subject: NyroHealth packaging: mapping features to lower tier & downgrade path
messages:
From: Maya Singh <maya@nyrohealth.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@nyrohealth.com>
Date: Sat, 29 Jul 2028 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Packaging question: downgrade path + feature mapping

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was impressed by the latency and the audit controls. Before we move to legal, Procurement asked for a clear explanation of how features map to tiers and what happens if NyroHealth needs to downgrade mid-year. A couple of specific asks: 

- Can you provide a one-page mapping of which features are in Tier A vs Tier B vs Tier C (we mainly care about embedding caching, prefix-KV retention, and priority routing)?
- If we downgrade from Tier A to Tier B during a quarter, what happens to: credits, SLA commitments, and any feature-gated capabilities?
- Are there any hard cutover windows or prorated refunds/credits?

We attached our internal SOW (placeholder) and a short feature list for reference. Ideally want something we can attach to the procurement packet.

Appreciate a pragmatic answer — procurement tends to escalate small unknowns.

Best,
Maya

Attachments: NyroHealth_SOW_v2.pdf (pdf, 212 KB), feature-list.csv (csv)
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.com>
To: Maya Singh <maya@nyrohealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 31 Jul 2028 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Packaging question: downgrade path + feature mapping

Hi Maya — thanks, and glad the demo went well. I pulled together a short mapping and the downgrade policy below; attaching a concise feature matrix for your procurement packet (NyroHealth_feature_matrix_v1.xlsx). High level answers first, then details: 

1) Feature mapping (summary): 
- Tier A (Enterprise): prefix-KV retention (30 days), priority routing, KV cache snapshot exports, SLA 99.95
- Tier B (Business): prefix-KV retention (7 days), best-effort routing, limited snapshot exports, SLA 99.9
- Tier C (Starter): prefix-KV retention (24 hours), no priority routing, no snapshot exports, SLA 99.5

2) Downgrade behavior (mid-term): 
- Credits: usage credits already consumed are not refunded. We perform prorated billing on committed components (reserved capacity) for the remaining billing period; see examples below.
- Features: feature gates that require persistent state (e.g., KV retention >7 days) will be disabled on downgrade; a read-only export of retained data is provided for 30 days to allow migration.
- SLA & routing: SLA targets will switch to the new tier level on the downgrade effective date; priority routing is removed immediately (no staged window).

3) Cutover windows / timing: 
- Downgrade request must be submitted 5 business days before the desired effective date to allow capacity reallocation.
- Proration: for Dedicated reserved capacity we prorate by day for the remainder of the month; for metered components we bill actual usage.

I put concrete examples in the attached workbook and below. Happy to walk procurement through it live.

Jasmine

Attachment: NyroHealth_feature_matrix_v1.xlsx
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Maya Singh <maya@nyrohealth.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 31 Jul 2028 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Packaging question: downgrade path + feature mapping

Maya — quick pricing notes to include in the packet. Examples below are illustrative; final numbers in the SOW and order form.

Example A (downgrade of reserved capacity mid-month):
- 1 month, Tier A reserved pool -> request to downgrade on day 12 of a 30-day billing period. We invoice Tier A for days 1–11, then Tier B for days 12–30 at Tier B daily rate. No retro credits for consumed tokens.

Example B (feature gated KV retention):
- If you relied on 30-day retention and downgrade to a tier with 7-day retention, we snapshot the 30-day KV store and provide a one-time export (CSV/NDJSON) accessible for 30 days. If you request restoration later, restoration is treated as a new import (charges apply).

Discounts/Concessions:
- For committed deals we can offer a conversion credit if you extend committed months beyond original term; any one-off concessions require manager approval (looping Laura).

If Procurement wants an explicit clause for migration assistance and export timelines we can add a one-paragraph addendum.

Thanks,
Ben
From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.com>, Maya Singh <maya@nyrohealth.com>
Date: Mon, 31 Jul 2028 10:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Packaging question: downgrade path + feature mapping

Thanks for the clear write-up everyone. Maya — we can grant a limited migration concession: if NyroHealth signs the initial 12-month commit at Tier A we will include a one-time migration credit equal to 10% of the first month’s committed reserved capacity to help offset any data-migration or re-ingestion costs in the event of a downgrade within the first 90 days. We will also add the one-paragraph migration assistance addendum Ben mentioned.

Conditions: credit applies only to reserved capacity (not metered tokens), and requires a formal downgrade request window (5 business days). Legal will add exact language.

Laura
VP, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Maya Singh <maya@nyrohealth.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 31 Jul 2028 11:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Packaging question: downgrade path + feature mapping

Team — this is perfect, thank you. Procurement asked for the one-line concession and the effective 5-business-day window; they also want the export process documented. Can you send a one-page summary and the short clause we can drop into the SOW? We'll attach the feature matrix and the SOW and push to Legal.

I'll mark next steps:

- Ben/Laura: confirm credit mechanics in writing for procurement packet

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

— Maya
